audio.strategy: Sampled multi-piano instrument with a live-DSP effect chain. Primary sound: three bundled RECORDED sample sets (Grand/Upright/Electric) played through AudioBufferSourceNodes with nearest-root selection, recorded-velocity-layer crossfading (grand) or declared gain+filter velocity shaping (single-layer sets), unison detune copies, and per-voice envelopes. One AudioContext: voices enter per-layer buses (timbre EQ, dynamic compression, level), then the ordered per-layer effect chain Mod 1 → Mod 2 → Delay → Amp Sim/EQ → Compressor → Reverb, then either the single Rotary Speaker instance (Amp unit 'To Rotary') or directly the master gain → limiter → one destination. All effects are live Web Audio processing (LFOs, modulated delays, biquads, waveshapers, convolution). The Phase 1 oscillator voice survives only as a clearly labeled synthesized fallback after primary sample failure.

sampleSources.name: Salamander Grand ('Grand' type)
sampleSources.source: Salamander Grand Piano V3 — Yamaha C5 recorded by Alexander Holm (archive.org/details/SalamanderGrandPianoV3), obtained exclusively through the npm registry packages @audio-samples/piano-mp3-velocity4, -velocity8 and -velocity13 (v1.0.5) and copied into public/samples/grand by scripts/sync-samples.mjs.
sampleSources.license: CC BY 3.0 — attribution: 'Salamander Grand Piano V3' by Alexander Holm.
files: public/samples/grand/<a0|c1|ds1|fs1…c8>-l<1|2|3>.mp3 — 30 root notes (A/C/D#/F# per octave, A0–C8) × 3 recorded velocity layers (Salamander layers 4, 8, 13 of 16) = 90 files; per-file roots/layers listed in public/samples/manifest.json
sampleSources.notes: Recorded velocity layers are crossfaded by played velocity. Decoded tails longer than 6.5 s are truncated with a fade to bound memory; this is declared processing of recorded material, not synthesis.

sampleSources.name: Tack Upright ('Upright' type)
sampleSources.source: GM Honky-tonk piano program (detuned tack-upright character), note-per-note mp3 renders from the MIDI-JS Soundfonts collection (github.com/gleitz/midi-js-soundfonts, Benjamin Gleitzman), obtained via the npm registry package web-music-score-samples v3.0.0 (samples/003-honkytonk-piano) and copied into public/samples/upright.
sampleSources.license: MIT (MIDI-JS Soundfonts collection; repackaged MIT by web-music-score-samples).
files: public/samples/upright/<c1|e1|gs1…c7>.mp3 — 19 root notes (C/E/Ab per octave) × 1 velocity layer
sampleSources.notes: The collection is rendered from the FluidR3_GM / MusyngKite / FatBoy soundfont banks; the packaging does not identify which bank produced these renders — declared honestly. Single recorded velocity layer: velocity response is shaped by gain and a velocity-keyed lowpass in the engine and is declared as such.

generatedSources.name: Synthesized fallback voice
generatedSources.notes: Used ONLY after primary sample failure (or a minimal reduced graph) and labeled 'FALLBACK … synthesized' in the status strip and Program display. Never presented as recorded material.

generatedSources.name: Reverb impulse responses
generatedSources.kind: algorithmically generated buffers (deterministic xorshift noise, per-type decay/predelay/spring character)
generatedSources.notes: Six reverb types use generated IRs through a ConvolverNode — generated DSP, not recorded spaces.

generatedSources.name: String-resonance impulse and pedal-noise thump
generatedSources.notes: String Res is a generated sympathetic-resonance approximation active with the damper lifted (the spec's pedal-down samples are not available); Ped Noise is a generated filtered thump. Both are declared approximations, never recordings.

generatedSources.name: Effect processing (Mod 1/Mod 2/Delay/Amp-EQ/Compressor/Rotary)
generatedSources.kind: live Web Audio DSP (LFO-modulated gains/panners/filters/delays, feedback delay loop with in-loop filtering, waveshaper drive, DynamicsCompressor, dual-band rotary with inertial speed ramps)
generatedSources.notes: Every unit processes real audio through connected nodes with click-free crossfaded bypass; no unit is a label, enum or disconnected node.

notes: All recorded material was obtained exclusively through the npm registry (the run's only permitted network source) and is bundled under public/samples/ for fully offline playback; see public/samples/SOURCES.md and scripts/sync-samples.mjs for the exact provenance chain.
One AudioContext feeds per-layer buses, ordered effects, the single rotary instance, master gain and limiter into one destination; no engine or effect creates a parallel context or destination.

Clav/Digital/Misc piano types have no bundled model: selecting them flashes the type LED and reports 'Piano not found' on the Program display, and the layer plays nothing rather than pretending (spec: nord-stage-4.piano.json selection.missingModelState).

Functional Phase 2 controls: keybed + pedals, full Piano section, full Layer Effects section (except the Synth FX-focus button, decorative until a Synth engine exists), Rotary strip (drive/speed/stop), Master Level, pitch stick (±2 semitones on Piano voices), Panic, and Shift as the Global-mode modifier. Organ, Synth and remaining Program/Morph controls stay truthfully decorative until Phase 3.

Deterministic tests cross the real audio boundary via node-web-audio-api OfflineAudioContext rendering (no network, devices or audio output); browser boundaries (context, assets, MIDI, timers) remain injectable and fake-backed state tests complement, not replace, the rendered-audio proofs.
